stories.headline: Samsung Foundry Reportedly Wins AMD 2nm CPU Order as TSMC Capacity Tightens

key_facts.fact: Korea's Daishin Securities estimated Samsung Foundry won a 2nm notebook CPU order from a 'North American fabless customer,' with the tipster Jukan and subsequent reports identifying AMD as the source.
key_facts.excerpt: Korea's Daishin Securities: Samsung Foundry is estimated to have won a 2nm notebook CPU order from a North American fabless customer... Jukan later posited that 'it looks like AMD.'

key_facts.fact: The order is expected to cover AMD's next-generation 2nm Venice and Verano CPUs, which had previously been positioned as TSMC-exclusive on the N2 node.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD appears to have settled on Samsung's chip fabrication arm to produce its next-gen 2nm CPUs, Venice and Verano... With TSMC's advanced node capacity choked till 2028, Samsung appears to be AMD's next best option.

key_facts.fact: Digitimes framed the shift as TSMC's AI grip loosening, with US chipmakers increasingly engaging Samsung and Intel as alternative suppliers.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI semiconductor supply chain is showing unexpected signs of a shift, with TSMC's long-held dominance in the foundry market beginning to loosen. US chipmakers are increasingly engaging with Samsung Electronics and Intel as alternative suppliers.

key_facts.fact: AMD CEO Lisa Su personally visited Samsung's Pyeongtaek foundry plant earlier this year as part of the evaluation.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD's Lisa Su visited Samsung's Pyeongtaek foundry plant not too long ago to personally undertake an evaluation of Samsung's capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's foundry chief Marco Chisari said in late April that the company is actively engaged in 2nm collaboration discussions with multiple major AI and HPC clients.
key_facts.excerpt: We are actively engaged in 2nm collaboration discussions with multiple major AI and HPC clients, and with some customers, we will demonstrate tangible results in the near future.

sources.title: Samsung Foundry Has Apparently Won A 2nm CPU Order From A 'North American Fabless Customer,' With AMD Identified As The Order's Source

Samsung Nears 2nm Foundry Deal With Major Clients, Tangible Results Imminent

stories.headline: Cerebras Raises IPO Price Range to $150-$160, Could Fetch $4.8B at Top of Range

key_facts.fact: Cerebras Systems is considering a new IPO price range of $150-$160 per share, up from $115-$125, and raising the number of shares marketed to 30 million from 28 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is considering a new IPO price range of $150-$160 a share, up from $115-$125 a share, and raising the number of shares marketed to 30 million from 28 million.

key_facts.fact: At the top of the new range, Cerebras would raise roughly $4.8 billion, up from $3.5 billion under its original terms.
key_facts.excerpt: At the top of the new range, Cerebras would raise roughly $4.8 billion, up from $3.5 billion under its original terms, though the figures remain subject to change before pricing.

key_facts.fact: The book is oversubscribed by more than 20 times, ahead of May 13 pricing; Bloomberg had previously reported a planned bump to $125-$135 per share.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras' IPO has drawn orders for more than 20 times the number of shares available, the people said, as the chipmaker looks to manage surging interest ahead of its May 13 pricing. Bloomberg News previously reported the company planned to raise the price range of the IPO to $125-$135 per share.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras makes wafer-scale chips optimized for AI inference; customers include Amazon and OpenAI, and the listing would be the biggest IPO globally so far this year per Dealogic.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras' chips are better suited for inference... Cerebras has secured Amazon and OpenAI, two of the biggest builders of AI infrastructure in the world, as customers. The listing would be the biggest IPO globally so far this year, according to Dealogic.

key_facts.fact: The offering is being led by Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays and UBS; shares are expected to trade on Nasdaq Global Select Market under symbol CBRS.
key_facts.excerpt: The offering is being led by Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays and UBS Group AG. Cerebras plans for its shares to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol CBRS.

stories.headline: SoftBank Launches Japan Battery Business Targeting GWh-Scale for AI Data Centers by FY2028

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Corp. on May 11 launched a Japan-based battery business aimed at building next-generation power infrastructure to support AI-driven electricity demand, covering development through manufacturing of battery cells and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank Corp. launched a Japan-based battery business aimed at building next-generation power infrastructure to support the rapidly increasing demand for electricity being driven by AI adoption.

key_facts.fact: The battery operation is anchored at the Osaka Sakai AI Data Center on a former Sharp LCD plant, with a 'GX Factory' targeting mass production at gigawatt-hour-per-year scale by FY2028.
key_facts.excerpt: At the GX Factory, SoftBank plans to begin manufacturing battery cells and energy storage systems from the fiscal year ending March 31, 2028 (FY2027), with the aim of achieving mass production on a gigawatt-hour (GWh)-per-year scale by around FY2028.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank is targeting over 100 billion JPY (~$640 million) in annual revenue from its domestic battery business by FY2030, with plans to expand into grid, industrial, residential and global markets.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank aims to achieve annual revenue of over 100 billion JPY for its domestic battery business by FY2030.

key_facts.fact: Nikkei reported SoftBank is partnering with South Korea's Cosmos Lab to commercialize zinc-halogen batteries that avoid lithium and cobalt, with first deployment at the Sakai data center.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank and Cosmos Lab plan to jointly develop zinc halide batteries and begin production in 2027... The mass-produced batteries will first be used at the large-scale data center that SoftBank is building on the Sakai site.

key_facts.fact: The Sakai AI Data Center is targeted to start at ~150 MW of power capacity in 2026, with planned expansion above 250 MW.
key_facts.excerpt: Begin operations of an AI data center with a power capacity of approximately 150 megawatts in 2026. In the future, we plan to expand the capacity to over 250 megawatts.

stories.headline: Microsoft-G42 $1B Kenya Data Center Stalled by Payment-Guarantee Dispute, Not Just Power

key_facts.fact: A major Microsoft-G42 data center site in East Africa has been delayed after the Kenyan government couldn't commit to annual capacity payments at the level Microsoft requested, breaking down the talks, Bloomberg reported on May 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft and its partner, Abu Dhabi-based tech conglomerate G42, had asked the government to commit to paying for a certain amount of capacity annually... When the government couldn't provide the guarantees at the level Microsoft requested, the talks broke down.

key_facts.fact: The $1 billion geothermal-powered facility near Olkaria, planned for ~100 km northwest of Nairobi, was announced during President Ruto's May 2024 visit to Washington with an original May 2026 target for phase-one operation.
key_facts.excerpt: Ruto had announced plans for the huge facility during a state visit to Washington in May 2024... it would run on geothermal power... once-hyped project had stalled.

key_facts.fact: President Ruto said the facility would have required a third of Kenya's ~3,000 MW installed capacity, telling grassroots leaders: 'To switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country.'
key_facts.excerpt: Ruto, speaking to grassroots leaders in Nairobi last week, said Kenya was forced to reconsider the plans after learning that it would require a third of the country's total installed capacity of around 3,000 megawatts. 'To switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country.'

key_facts.fact: Phase one was a 100 MW build, well within Olkaria's roughly 950 MW geothermal capacity, suggesting the binding obstacle was risk allocation on a multi-year dollar-denominated capacity guarantee rather than grid limits.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase one was 100 MW, and Olkaria's geothermal complex generates roughly 950 MW. Phase one was always within reach... The binding question on phase one was never really the power. It was who carried the risk if East African demand for Azure capacity took longer to materialise.

key_facts.fact: Officials said the project has not been cancelled, with ongoing discussions on restructuring power capacity and financing arrangements.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the delay, officials familiar with the talks said the project has not been cancelled, and discussions are ongoing on restructuring the deal, including power capacity and financing arrangements.

sources.title: Microsoft's African Data Center Falters on Payment Demands
It Wasn't Just the Grid. Microsoft Asked Kenya for a Cheque the Government Couldn't Write.
Energy shortfall 'problem' scuppers Kenya's $1B Microsoft data center

stories.headline: TrendForce: AI Demand Drives 3nm and 2.5D Packaging Into Critical Shortage

key_facts.fact: TrendForce says surging AI demand has tightened 3nm-2nm wafer and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging into capacity bottlenecks, with TSMC's 3nm capacity becoming a 'scarce resource fiercely contested by global tech giants.'
key_facts.excerpt: The surging AI demand is creating capacity bottlenecks in 3nm–2 nm wafers and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging, according to TrendForce... 3nm advanced process capacity—currently dominated by TSMC—has become even more constrained, turning into a scarce resource fiercely contested by global tech giants.

key_facts.fact: TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging has remained in short supply since 2023; TrendForce expects severe 2.5D packaging tightness to ease only slightly by 2027, aided by TSMC's plan to expand CoWoS capacity by over 60% by that year.
key_facts.excerpt: CoWoS has remained in short supply since 2023, prompting customers to seek alternative capacity sources... TrendForce expects that the severe shortage in global 2.5D packaging capacity will begin to ease slightly by 2027, aided by order spillover and TSMC's plan to expand CoWoS capacity by over 60% by 2027.

key_facts.fact: AI compute chips are migrating from 4nm to 3nm in late 2025 and 2026 while smartphones and PCs have yet to shift en masse to 2nm, concentrating high-performance demand on 3nm.
key_facts.excerpt: AI compute chips are rapidly transitioning from 4nm to 3nm between late 2025 and 2026. At the same time, high-end smartphone and PC processors have yet to migrate en masse to the next-generation 2nm node, resulting in a short-term concentration of high-performance demand on 3nm.

key_facts.fact: Samsung and Intel remain behind TSMC in 3nm progress, producing a 'temporary single-supplier dynamic dominated by TSMC,' with global 3nm capacity expected to surpass 5/4nm by year-end 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung and Intel remain behind TSMC in 3 nm foundry progress... this has led to a temporary single-supplier dynamic dominated by TSMC... global 3nm capacity is expected to surpass 5/4nm by the end of 2026 and become the second-largest process node after 28nm by 2027.

key_facts.fact: Alternative packaging technologies like Intel's EMIB and FOEB are gaining traction, while SPIL and Amkor have benefited from CoWoS shortages.
key_facts.excerpt: Providers such as SPIL and Amkor have benefited from this, and alternative technologies like EMIB and FOEB are also gaining traction, with Intel leveraging its U.S.-based manufacturing advantage.

sources.title: TrendForce Sees Tightening Advanced Packaging and 3nm Capacity as AI Competition Turns Into a Supply Chain Arms Race

stories.headline: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon: 2026 is Year of AI Agents and End of Smartphone-Centric World

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon told Fortune that 2026 is the year AI agents become mainstream and that the smartphone's reign as the primary consumer device is coming to an end.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon has stated that 2026 will be the year that AI agents become mainstream, with the smartphone's role as primary device for consumers... ending.

key_facts.fact: Amon framed Qualcomm's reinvention from a smartphone-dependent chipmaker into automotive, robotics, and wearable AI form factors — glasses, jewelry, pins, pendants — designed to connect users to an agent.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm's success in part to its culture of reinvention, which has evolved from being highly smartphone-dependent to working in automotive robotics and wearable AI jewelry, pins, pendants, and other things that can connect users to an agent.

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is targeting roughly $22 billion in non-mobile revenue by 2029, with 6G framed as the wireless transition to AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: His vision for the future of personal AI devices, with a focus on the non-mobile business towards a projected $22 billion by 2029... the potential of 6G internet as a wireless transition to AI agents.

key_facts.fact: In a separate Fortune interview May 9, Amon said Qualcomm is working with 'pretty much all' major AI players on top-secret devices and is powering OpenAI's first push into hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm's CEO is working with 'pretty much all' major AI players on top-secret devices—and powering OpenAI's first push into hardware... Cristiano Amon's pitch is that the smartphone-centric world Qualcomm helped build is coming to an end.

sources.title: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon says 2026 is the year AI agents go mainstream—and the smartphone's reign as your primary device is ending
Qualcomm's CEO is working with 'pretty much all' major AI players on top-secret devices
